preRegistration.text:
# Pre-registration: WASP-52 b, MicroObservatory night of 2026-09-13 UT

Written by hand (mobs_night wrote no scaffold: its verdict was REJECT on the seed floor) and committed BEFORE any fit.

Frames: 78, 03:45 to 07:37 UT, 60 s Clear.
Archive (NEA pscomppars, fetched 2026-09-13 09:2x UTC): P 1.74977980 d, T0 2455793.681430, T14 1.810 h,
Rp/Rs 0.1646 (depth 2.71%), V 12.192. Epoch 3145: predicted Tmid 2461296.73890 (05:44 UT), ingress 04:49,
egress 06:38; 64 min pre-ingress and 59 min post-egress in the window (full transit by geometry).
Propagated ephemeris bar 5.6 min.

Why this night runs at all. The tool's verdict was REJECT: seed target 197 ADU above a 410 background in frame 1,
under the 300 ADU floor I set after WASP-80/Qatar-1/TrES-5 (peak-pixel measure). But frame 1 is graded clear at 76%
of the night's clear reference (aperture flux 1491 of 1969 ADU), so on the clearest frames the peak would be ~260 ADU:
the target is AT the floor, not under it by cloud. V 12.19 is exactly the "V~12 or brighter" line I gave Rob on 09-05.
A full transit with a 2.71% depth on a target at the line is the first direct test of whether the floor is set right.
That is the reason for --force, stated before the fit. The floor stays as my own filter either way; this is a
calibration point for it, not a challenge to anyone's upload.

Sky, from the triage (stars per frame and the target's aperture flux, not the background):
- pre-ingress 22 frames: clear 1, partial 9, lost 12 (04:06-04:45 UT, target flux 0-40% of reference). The sky
  clears at 04:48-04:51, i.e. AT ingress. There is effectively no clean pre-ingress baseline.
- in-transit 36 frames: clear 34, partial 2.
- post-egress 20 frames: clear 12, partial 8.
So the fit is anchored by the in-transit bottom, egress, and the post-egress baseline; ingress itself is
in the first clear frames.

Predictions:
1. EXOTIC finds and follows the target from frame 1 without losing the centroid (aperture flux is ~10x the
   WASP-80/Qatar-1 cases that set the floor). If it loses the star, the 300 ADU floor stands as written and this
   night is a rejection with no timing claim.
2. Scatter from the V calibration (0.84% at V 11.57, photon scaling): ~1.12% (scatter/depth 0.41). On the
   in-transit and post frames I expect that or a little worse (1.1-1.5%); the 12 lost pre-ingress frames will be
   outliers or clipped, not a baseline.
3. Tmid bar 10-16 min: an egress-anchored fit, roughly 1.5-2x the 8 min a full clear night at this ratio would give.
   Under 8 min from the printed posterior is a replaced bar (#1401) and gets the independent refit before the ledger.
   Over 25 min: the pre-ingress cloud did more damage than the counts show.
4. Tmid within that bar of 2461296.73890. A miss of more than one bar on an egress-anchored fit says the
   pre-ingress cloud biased the baseline, not that the ephemeris is off (5.6 min bar).
5. Depth within 1 sigma of 2.71%, but with a bar larger than usual; the likely failure mode is a depth biased HIGH
   (cloudy pre-ingress frames where comp ratios do not fully remove the extinction). If the depth comes out more
   than 1 sigma high with the pre-ingress residuals visibly structured, that is the reading, not a discovery.
6. QC verdict: MARGINAL more likely than PASS, because of the pre-ingress residuals; FAIL would mean prediction 1 or
   2 failed.
7. Frames are run AS-IS first (all 78, what an ordinary user would upload). The 12 lost frames are set aside for a
   second run ONLY if EXOTIC cannot align or crashes on them, never to improve the answer; if that happens the
   record says so.
- Any printed bar under 0.001 d is a replaced bar (#1401) and gets refit before the ledger.
- First-frame coordinates from a local plate solve; drift by star-pair voting; comps in the triage box within
  1.8-4.9x the target; #1409 confirms the rest. exotic -pf PASS, check_inits PASS.
- Not submitted regardless; checkpoint holds.

parameters.Fit parameter point estimate: Best-fit likelihood point; uncertainties are posterior spread.
parameters.Prefit refinement note: Using an initial nested fit to estimate a transit duration of 0.075911 day(s), kept the full light curve because no extra baseline points fell outside the target window, and setting the second-pass Tmid bounds to [2461296.708654, 2461296.784565].
parameters.Pre-UltraNest LM boundary scout note: LM solution and covariance envelope were interior after 4 iteration(s).
parameters.Out-of-transit baseline parameter-fit no: Not used in the final refit because the out-of-transit linear detrending already flattened the final-fit flux baseline.
parameters.Out-of-transit baseline detrending note: Applied weighted linear out-of-transit baseline detrending using 16 pre-ingress and 13 post-egress points.
parameters.Sparse posterior live-point extension no: Applied additive selected comparison-star final UltraNest extension (200->1200 minimum live points).
parameters.Final residual rejection note: No residual outliers exceeded 3.0 sigma from the iterated median residual (0.3647%, stdev=1.8233%).
parameters.Uncertainty interpretation note: The primary Rp/R* and radius-ratio area-depth uncertainties use model+red-noise when available. The red-noise uncertainty inflates the data-fit standard error by a residual time-binning beta factor before combining it with the model posterior. The flux baseline red-noise uncertainty is the out-of-transit baseline component used for the final-plot baseline band; the transit-depth red-noise uncertainty already includes both the in-transit and baseline terms. The same residual time-binning beta factor is applied to the posterior uncertainties for Tmid, a/Rs, inclination, and impact parameter when reporting their primary model+red-noise uncertainties. The flux-scatter equivalent is also shown as a diagnostic of the full residual scatter around the model.
